bull.b: Revenue growth and a richer mix toward higher-value T-Rex and Balance wearables indicate improving product positioning. Higher gross margin suggests premiumization can support better unit economics and strengthen the company’s earnings potential over the next several quarters.

Reaching a top-six value-share position in two major regions provides evidence of growing brand relevance and distribution strength. Continued share gains can improve scale, increase ecosystem adoption, and create a more durable platform for future hardware and service growth.

The multi-year HYROX partnership broadens Zepp’s presence beyond device sales by linking hardware, training content, software, and performance data. This can deepen user engagement, differentiate Amazfit from generic wearables, and support sustained ecosystem loyalty.

bear.b: Despite improved gross margin and narrower losses, Zepp has not restored sustainable profitability. Continuing operating and net losses constrain internal funding, reduce resilience during weaker demand, and make the planned return to profitable growth dependent on execution over coming quarters.

Repeated negative operating and free cash flow show that the business has not consistently funded operations internally. If losses continue, cash burn could require further balance-sheet support, limiting investment flexibility and increasing the financial consequences of execution setbacks.

Higher spending and foreign-exchange pressure are limiting the conversion of revenue growth into earnings. Even with a richer product mix and improved gross margin, persistent cost intensity could delay breakeven and make profitability more sensitive to operating or currency changes.
